messages:
Mara: Quick thread — we saw a spike in tokenized traffic during the load test and a lot of keys hit short bursts. Current behavior is immediate 429s. I'm leaning toward a small "grace period" that surfaces soft backpressure (Retry-After + heuristic queueing) before we start hard-shedding. Thoughts?

Devin: +1 to trying a short grace window. Users see 429s as fatal; if we can absorb a 1-3s burst it's better UX. But we need to be careful about tail latency impact.

Jonathan: Agreed but we must bound memory. If we queue too many requests we'll OOM the workers. Any queuing needs a strict max size and eviction policy by per-key priority.

Priya: Can we make it per-key vs per-org? Some product keys (e.g., embedding pipelines) are noisy but org-level limits should still protect tenant isolation.

Mara: Plan: token-bucket per-key + burst credits + a graceful short-queue that accepts requests for up to grace_window_secs. After that, either reject (429) or return 503 if we are system-overloaded. Also surface a new metric: "queued_vs_rejected" per-route.

Devin: +1 for both metrics and making reject type conditional. Implementation idea: if queueing is due to per-key burst, return 429 with Retry-After. If queueing is due to global capacity (worker pool full), return 503 to indicate infra problem.

sam: Question — how do clients detect which to back off on? Some SDKs implement automatic retries on 429 only. If we use 503 for infra, SDKs should retry differently. We should document expected semantics in the SDK.

Priya: Also we should emit a header so clients can make smarter decisions: e.g., `X-RateLimit-Mode: grace|throttle|unavailable` and `Retry-After` when applicable.

Mara: Draft config snippet I'm proposing for the limiter:
```yaml
rate_limit:
  per_key:
    capacity: 1000   # tokens
    refill_per_sec: 200
    burst_credits: 300
  grace_window_secs: 2    # allow soft-queue for N seconds
  max_queue_per_worker: 128
  queue_eviction: "oldest_key_first"
  fallback_status: 
    per_key_exhaustion: 429
    global_overload: 503
```

Jonathan: That looks reasonable. For `queue_eviction` maybe prefer priority eviction (drop lowest-priority requests first) — but ok to start with oldest. Also force a hard cap on memory used by queued request metadata.

Devin: We also need to ensure batching/continuous-inference paths aren't adversely affected. If a queued request waits for >grace_window but is part of a batch, we might increase latency for the whole batch. Suggest we exclude cross-batch streaming routes from soft-queueing and always apply immediate shedding there.

Priya: UX ask: Console should show per-key burst debt and queued_count over time so customers understand why requests are being delayed. Add a health signal for "grace_saturation" to alerts.

Mara: Ops-bot fired earlier alert: "rate_limiter: keys_exhausted=23 global_queue=110" — saw it during test. ops-bot: any logs retained?

ops-bot: Saved alert context to https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-112. Attached sample keys and timeline.

sam: Action items I'm volunteering for:
- Implement per-key bucket + burst credits (feature-flagged)
- Add headers `X-RateLimit-Mode` and `Retry-After` semantics in SDKs
- Instrument `queued_vs_rejected`, `grace_saturation`, `queue_evictions` as metrics

Jonathan: I'll help with memory safeguards + eviction logic and mark routes that are queue-ineligible.

Devin: I'll wire up dashboard tiles and alerts, plus a short runbook blurb describing 429 vs 503 semantics. Link to runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/rate-limiter (draft).

Priya: Note: for Dedicated customers we may want different defaults (longer grace window or larger burst credits). Add config knobs per-deployment.

Mara: Consensus seems to be: soft-grace-window first (per-key), immediate shedding for queue-ineligible routes, 429 for per-key exhaustion, 503 for cluster/global overload, headers for client behavior, metrics + console UX. I'll open a PR with the initial config and a feature flag.

Devin: :thumbsup: Please include a small perf test that simulates many small bursts so we can validate no tail-latency regression.

Mara: Will do. PR ETA EOD tomorrow.

sam: Sounds good. I'll add SDK notes after the PR lands.

Priya: Thanks everyone.
